discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller, with Jaksch and co-workers, proposed in 1998 that cold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with fully tunable parameters. In 2002 Greiner and Bloch observed the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator, which opened the experimental field of analog quantum simulation. Since then the three have turned this idea into a precise laboratory tool. Quantum gas microscopes resolve single atoms and spins. Experiments have revealed antiferromagnetic order and hidden correlations in the Fermi-Hubbard model, many-body localization, and topological band properties, and they measure entanglement entropy directly. These are questions that are hard to settle in solids or with classical computers. Their work founded a worldwide research field and underpins today's neutral-atom quantum processors. It shows how controlled quantum matter yields clean answers about strongly correlated systems.
